cases.name: simple_valid
cases.note: a decision line after free-text reasoning is read; the reasoning itself is not
cases.text:
Option A sounds tempting, but B has the better expected value.
DECISION: B

cases.name: reasoning_never_read
cases.note: no DECISION: line at all -> unparseable, even though the prose clearly picks B
cases.text: Option A is tempting, but in the end I go with B.

cases.name: repeated_same_token_valid
cases.note: the SAME token restated on two lines is repetition, not ambiguity
cases.text:
DECISION: A
To be clear, restating: DECISION: A

cases.name: conflicting_tokens_unparseable
cases.note: two DIFFERENT tokens on separate lines is a real conflict, rejected outright

cases.name: token_not_in_options
cases.note: a well-formed decision line naming an option that does not exist

cases.name: empty_string
cases.note: an empty response is its own outcome, distinct from unparseable

cases.name: whitespace_only
cases.note: whitespace-only text counts as empty, not as a response with no decision line

cases.name: none_text
cases.note: no text content at all (e.g. an empty completion) is empty, same as ""

cases.name: markdown_emphasis_stripped
cases.note: **bold** markers around the decision line are stripped before matching

cases.name: trailing_punctuation_stripped
cases.note: a trailing period after the token is stripped, not treated as part of the token

cases.name: fullwidth_colon_and_extra_spaces
cases.note: a fullwidth colon and collapsed internal whitespace both still match the grammar

cases.name: greek_letters_not_normalized
cases.note: no script normalization: Greek capital Alpha (U+0391) is a different token from Latin 'A', not a look-alike to fold
cases.text:
Η λογική λέει Β, αλλά επιλέγω:
DECISION: Α

cases.name: case_insensitive_keyword
cases.note: the keyword 'decision' and the token are matched case-insensitively (casefold)
